2.10.1. When a game value is a negative number, it is treated as 0 for all references and comparisons of values.

> **EXAMPLE:** A Unit has 2 power. An effect reduces its power by 3. The Unit has -1 power, but is treated as having 0 power when attacking, fighting, or when a card effect references its power. 4.12.1. When a Gear moves with a Unit or Legend to an area outside of the field or Legends area, the Gear isn’t equipped to the Unit or Legend in that area.

rules.text: 10.6.1. If all of an effect is invalid, ignore that effect.

rules.title: If part of an effect is invalid, ignore the invalid part and resolve as much of the remaining effect as possible.
rules.text: 10.6.2. If part of an effect is invalid, ignore the invalid part and resolve as much of the remaining effect as possible.

rules.title: Even if an effect is invalid, it is still considered an effect on the card.
rules.text: 10.6.3. Even if an effect is invalid, it is still considered an effect on the card.

rules.title: If an activated effect requires a target or choice as part of activation cost but no legal target or choice exists, t…
rules.text: 10.8. If an activated effect requires a target or choice as part of activation cost but no legal target or choice exists, the effect is invalid and you cannot activate it.

rules.title: If an effect becomes invalid after it activates or becomes pending, still resolve as much of the effect as possible.
rules.text: 10.10. If an effect becomes invalid after it activates or becomes pending, still resolve as much of the effect as possible.

rules.title: If resolving a pending effect requires information about a game piece that is no longer valid, use the information fr…
rules.text: 10.10.1. If resolving a pending effect requires information about a game piece that is no longer valid, use the information from when the piece was last valid.

rules.title: A “pending” effect is an effect that is waiting to resolve.
rules.text: 10.11. A “pending” effect is an effect that is waiting to resolve.

rules.title: You cannot take any game actions until all pending effects are resolved.
rules.text: 10.11.1. You cannot take any game actions until all pending effects are resolved.

rules.title: Once an effect becomes pending, it remains pending until it resolves or a rule or effect removes it from pending.
rules.text: 10.11.2. Once an effect becomes pending, it remains pending until it resolves or a rule or effect removes it from pending.

rules.title: After a pending effect resolves, it stops being pending.
rules.text: 10.11.3. After a pending effect resolves, it stops being pending.

rules.title: If you have multiple pending effects, you may resolve them in any order.
rules.text: 10.12. If you have multiple pending effects, you may resolve them in any order.

rules.title: If both players control pending effects at the same time, the turn player resolves all their pending effects before t…
rules.text: 10.13. If both players control pending effects at the same time, the turn player resolves all their pending effects before their Rival resolves all of theirs.

rules.title: If a new effect triggers while resolving one, the new effect enters pending too.
rules.text: 10.14. If a new effect triggers while resolving one, the new effect enters pending too. Finish resolving the current pending effect before resolving any new pending effects.

rules.title: If both players have a new effect enter pending while resolving an effect, the player currently resolving pending eff…
rules.text: 10.14.1. If both players have a new effect enter pending while resolving an effect, the player currently resolving pending effects finishes resolving all of their pending effects (including the new ones) before their Rival resolves their new ones.

rules.title: Cost
A “cost” details what you must pay to play a card, activate an effect, or perform a game action.
rules.text: 11.1.1. A “cost” details what you must pay to play a card, activate an effect, or perform a game action. See Pay.

rules.title: To play a card, you must pay its cost value in the top left corner of the card.
rules.text: 11.1.1.1. To play a card, you must pay its cost value in the top left corner of the card. See Cost Value.

rules.title: An activation cost is a cost that must be paid to activate an effect.
rules.text: 11.1.1.2. An activation cost is a cost that must be paid to activate an effect. See EFFECTS > Activated Effects.

rules.title: A cost must be paid in full; if you cannot pay all required costs, you cannot play the card, activate the effect, nor…
rules.text: 11.1.2. A cost must be paid in full; if you cannot pay all required costs, you cannot play the card, activate the effect, nor perform the game action associated with it

rules.title: If a cost is replaced by another cost, pay the replacement cost instead of the original cost.
rules.text: 11.1.2.1. If a cost is replaced by another cost, pay the replacement cost instead of the original cost. The replacement cost must be paid in full.

rules.title: Lag
Lag is a condition applied to Units when they enter the field.
rules.text: 11.3.1. Lag is a condition applied to Units when they enter the field. Units with Lag are also called “lagging.”

rules.title: Lagging Units can’t attack.
rules.text: 11.3.1.1. Lagging Units can’t attack.

rules.title: Lagging Units can’t activate [Spend Icon] effects.
rules.text: 11.3.1.2. Lagging Units can’t activate [Spend Icon] effects.

rules.title: At the end of each turn, all Units lose the “Lag” condition.
rules.text: 11.3.2. At the end of each turn, all Units lose the “Lag” condition.

rules.title: Play
To play a card, reveal it, pay its cost, and then follow the rules for playing that specific card type detailed in {C…
rules.text: 11.4.1. To play a card, reveal it, pay its cost, and then follow the rules for playing that specific card type detailed in CARD TYPES.

rules.title: If you can’t pay for or follow the rules for playing the card, you cannot play it.
rules.text: 11.4.1.1. If you can’t pay for or follow the rules for playing the card, you cannot play it. It’s considered “invalid” to play.

rules.title: If you play or attempt to play an invalid card, undo the play attempt and return the game to the previous legal game…
rules.text: 11.4.1.2. If you play or attempt to play an invalid card, undo the play attempt and return the game to the previous legal game state as much as possible.

rules.title: You can only play cards from your hand unless an effect instructs otherwise.
rules.text: 11.4.2. You can only play cards from your hand unless an effect instructs otherwise.

rules.title: Effects that allow a player to play a card follows the normal rules for playing that card unless the effect instructs…
rules.text: 11.4.3. Effects that allow a player to play a card follows the normal rules for playing that card unless the effect instructs otherwise.

rules.title: Draw
“Draw” is a game action in which you move the top card of your deck to your hand.
rules.text: 11.5.1. “Draw” is a game action in which you move the top card of your deck to your hand.

rules.title: When an effect says “Draw X” (where X is a number), take the draw action X number of times.
rules.text: 11.5.2. When an effect says “Draw X” (where X is a number), take the draw action X number of times. Literally, it means “move the top card of your deck to your hand, X individual times.”

rules.title: When you “Draw X,” draw each card individually.
rules.text: 11.5.2.1. When you “Draw X,” draw each card individually. Do not take multiple cards from the top of your deck at once.

rules.title: When you “Draw up to X,” choose the number of cards you will draw, then draw exactly that number of cards.
rules.text: 11.5.2.2. When you “Draw up to X,” choose the number of cards you will draw, then draw exactly that number of cards.

rules.title: If you attempt to draw more cards than remain in your deck, it counts as drawing from an empty deck.
rules.text: 11.5.2.3. If you attempt to draw more cards than remain in your deck, it counts as drawing from an empty deck. See GAME OVERVIEW > Lose Conditions.

rules.title: Equip
“Equip” is a game action in which you attach a Gear to a Unit or Legend by placing the card beneath it.
rules.text: 11.6.1. “Equip” is a game action in which you attach a Gear to a Unit or Legend by placing the card beneath it. When you do, the Gear becomes “equipped to” that card. See CARD TYPES > Gear.

rules.title: When a Gear is equipped make sure only the bottom text box is showing under the equipped card.
rules.text: 11.6.1.1. When a Gear is equipped make sure only the bottom text box is showing under the equipped card.

rules.title: Gear stays equipped unless it (or the Unit/Legend it’s equipped to) is defeated or moves outside of the Legends area…
rules.text: 11.6.1.2. Gear stays equipped unless it (or the Unit/Legend it’s equipped to) is defeated or moves outside of the Legends area or field.

rules.title: A Unit or Legend with one or more Gears attached is “equipped.”
rules.text: 11.6.2. A Unit or Legend with one or more Gears attached is “equipped.”

rules.title: A Unit or Legend with no Gear attached is “unequipped.”
rules.text: 11.6.3. A Unit or Legend with no Gear attached is “unequipped.”

rules.title: Units and Legends inherit all effects in the bottom textbox of their equipped Gears.
rules.text: 11.6.4. Units and Legends inherit all effects in the bottom textbox of their equipped Gears.

rules.title: Units and Legends gain the power of their equipped Gears.
rules.text: 11.6.5. Units and Legends gain the power of their equipped Gears.

rules.title: "Move" is a game action in which you unequip a Gear from the Unit or Legend it’s equipped to and equip it to another…
rules.text: 11.6.6. "Move" is a game action in which you unequip a Gear from the Unit or Legend it’s equipped to and equip it to another valid Unit or Legend.

rules.title: Pay
“Pay” is a game action in which you spend a number of Eddies and/or Legends in the Legends area equal to a cost.
rules.text: 11.8.1. “Pay” is a game action in which you spend a number of Eddies and/or Legends in the Legends area equal to a cost.

rules.title: Effects that reduce the amount you pay to play a card or activate an effect do not change the card’s cost value, nor…
rules.text: 11.8.2. Effects that reduce the amount you pay to play a card or activate an effect do not change the card’s cost value, nor the activation cost value.

rules.title: Effects that reduce the amount you pay to play a card or activate an effect cannot reduce the amount below 1.
rules.text: 11.8.3. Effects that reduce the amount you pay to play a card or activate an effect cannot reduce the amount below 1.

rules.title: When you play a card “for Free,” play the card without paying its cost.
rules.text: 11.8.4. When you play a card “for Free,” play the card without paying its cost.

rules.title: When playing a card for free, you must still meet any additional conditions outside of the cost.
rules.text: 11.8.4.1. When playing a card for free, you must still meet any additional conditions outside of the cost.

rules.title: [Spend Icon] (Spend Icon)
rules.text: 11.15. ### [Spend Icon] (Spend Icon)

rules.title: The [Spend Icon] symbol is shorthand for an activation cost.
rules.text:
11.15.1. The [Spend Icon] symbol is shorthand for an activation cost. It means: “Spend this Unit or Legend to activate the following effect.”

> **EXAMPLE:** A friendly Unit has the effect “[Spend Icon] Draw 1.” The [Spend Icon] symbol is an activation trigger. You must specifically spend this Unit as a cost. If you do, you draw a card.

rules.title: To activate a [Spend Icon] effect, you must spend the card with the express purpose of paying its activation cost.
rules.text: 11.15.2. To activate a [Spend Icon] effect, you must spend the card with the express purpose of paying its activation cost. When you spend a Unit or Legend with this symbol for any other reason, it does not trigger the [Spend Icon] effect.

rules.title: After paying the cost to use a [Spend Icon] effect, immediately resolve the effect.
rules.text: 11.15.3. After paying the cost to use a [Spend Icon] effect, immediately resolve the effect.

rules.title: If a [Spend Icon] effect also has a condition, the condition must be met at the time of activation and resolution.
rules.text: 11.15.3.1. If a [Spend Icon] effect also has a condition, the condition must be met at the time of activation and resolution.

rules.title: If additional effects conditions are met in the process of using a [Spend Icon:] effect, resolve the [Spend Icon] eff…
rules.text: 11.15.3.2. If additional effects conditions are met in the process of using a [Spend Icon:] effect, resolve the [Spend Icon] effect, then resolve any other pending effects.

rules.title: “X €$” (where X is a number) denotes Eddies and/or Legends spent to pay a cost.
rules.text: 11.16.1. “X €$” (where X is a number) denotes Eddies and/or Legends spent to pay a cost.

rules.title: When bolded and preceding a colon, before the effect text, it represents an activation cost (or part of an activation…
rules.text:
11.16.1.1. When bolded and preceding a colon, before the effect text, it represents an activation cost (or part of an activation cost) for the effect. It means: “Pay X to activate the following effect.”

> **EXAMPLE:** A friendly Legend has the text “1 €$, [Spend Icon] Give a friendly Unit +1 power this turn for each of its equipped Gear.“ So, to activate this effect, you must spend this Legend and 1 other Eddie or Legend.

rules.title: [ATTACK]
The [ATTACK] trigger is shorthand for “When this Unit attacks, [...]”
rules.text: 11.21.1. The [ATTACK] trigger is shorthand for “When this Unit attacks, [...]”

rules.title: The effect attached to the [ATTACK] trigger enters pending when you spend the Unit for the purpose of declaring an at…
rules.text: 11.21.2. The effect attached to the [ATTACK] trigger enters pending when you spend the Unit for the purpose of declaring an attack.

rules.title: Any effects triggered by spending this Unit enter pending at the same time as any [ATTACK] effect(s).
rules.text: 11.21.2.1. Any effects triggered by spending this Unit enter pending at the same time as any [ATTACK] effect(s). See EFFECTS.

rules.title: Resolve all pending [ATTACK] effects before your Rival’s react step.
rules.text: 11.21.2.2. Resolve all pending [ATTACK] effects before your Rival’s react step. See ATTACK, FIGHT, AND STEAL > React Step.

rules.title: [BLOCKER]
The [BLOCKER] keyword is shorthand for “When a rival Unit attacks, you may spend this Unit to redirect the attack to…
rules.text: 11.24.1. The [BLOCKER] keyword is shorthand for “When a rival Unit attacks, you may spend this Unit to redirect the attack to it instead.“

rules.title: Activate [BLOCKER] as a reaction during the React Step of your Rival’s attack action.
rules.text: 11.24.2. Activate [BLOCKER] as a reaction during the React Step of your Rival’s attack action.

rules.title: When a Unit uses [BLOCKER], it becomes the target of the attacking Unit’s current attack.
rules.text: 11.24.3. When a Unit uses [BLOCKER], it becomes the target of the attacking Unit’s current attack.

faqs.question: Can a Legend in the field use its [Spend Icon:] effect the turn that it was played to the field area?
Can I use a Unit's [Spend Icon:] effect the turn it's played?
Can I play this card without a rival Unit on the field?
Can I choose a Unit that's already spent for this card's effect?
When I spend a Unit equipped with Zetatech Faceplate to declare an attack, do I get Zetatech Faceplate's effect before or after I resolve the attack?
faqs.answer: Before. Adjust the Gig for Zetatech Faceplate's effect before moving on to your Rival's react step.

faqs.question: If I spend a Unit equipped with Zetatech Faceplate to declare an attack, and the Unit or Legend has an [ATTACK] effect, do I get Zetatech Faceplacte's effect before or after the [ATTACK] effect?
faqs.answer: You can choose the order you resolve these effects.

faqs.question: If I spend a Unit or Legend equipped with Zetatech Faceplate to activate the Unit/Legend's [Spend Icon:] effect, do I get Zetatech Faceplate's effect before or after the activated effect?
faqs.answer: After. Resolve the activated [Spend Icon:] effect first.

faqs.question: If I spend a Legend equipped with Zetatech Faceplate to pay a card's cost, do I get Zetatech Faceplate's effect before or after I play the card?
faqs.answer: After. Play the card first, then adjust the Gig.

decisions.spent: Corporate Surveillance FAQ explicitly permits an already-SPENT target. Such selection resolves without a new readiness transition or CARD_SPENT fact; READY transitions to SPENT.
decisions.noTarget: Card FAQ explicitly permits play with no rival Unit. Resolve as much as possible; no forced invented target.
decisions.cost: 3.11.1.2: payment reductions/increases do not change cost value. Read immutable numeric cost, not payment contribution. 3.11.2.3 explicitly references a Legend DASH/Null cost as0, without changing or making it payable. Other nonnumeric costs remain null.
decisions.fieldLegend: 4.2.1: effective LEGEND+UNIT on field. Real admitted Goro/V cost5 are excluded by threshold, not type. Null-cost Legends cannot be played to the field under4.5.3; no such real positive path is admitted.
decisions.lag: 11.3 restricts attack and Spend-icon activation, not an external spend effect. Preserve Lag, Gear, identity, location and modifiers.
decisions.future: Faceplate FAQs are extension-point review only. No WHEN_SPENT source is admitted and no old payment/attack/Blocker/Spend-icon path is refactored.
